# Known limitations

Each item says what happens. Where a failure is silent, it says so.

## Reading PDFs

* **Scanned (image-only) PDFs** are rejected as `failed` ("no extractable text"). No OCR.
* **Only text PDFs generated by one library (ReportLab) were tested.** Real statements add
logos, watermarks, rotated text, landscape pages, multi-column page layouts and odd fonts.
None of these was tested.
* **Cells are split at a fixed 5pt gap.** Tightly packed columns can merge into one cell, and
large-font headings split into several cells.
* **Page furniture** (repeating headers/footers) is detected only in the top and bottom 60pt and
only when the exact text repeats on 2+ pages (page numbers are normalised). A running header
on one page of a two-page document cannot be told apart from content; the engine skips a
lone line at the top of a new page only if a data row or the repeated header follows it.
* **Wrapped names** are joined by geometry (a line less than 0.75 line-heights below the previous
one) plus content (text columns only). In a tightly spaced table, a name wrapped *above* its
row is attached to the *previous* row. Wrapped numeric cells are not supported.
* **Subtotal rows inside a table** are read as data unless named in `stop_at`, which ends the
whole table. Validation usually flags the resulting total mismatch.
* **A security whose name starts with a `stop_at` word** (e.g. "Total Systems" with stop word
"Total") ends the table early.
* **A header that reappears after the table ended is rejected** as ambiguous, so a statement
with opening and closing holdings under an identical header fails loudly.
* **Two columns whose x-ranges overlap** can misplace a cell. The engine errors when two cells
land in one column, but not when a single cell lands in the wrong one.
* **Excel and CSV statements are not supported.** One PDF holding several clients' statements is
not split (an email with several PDFs is handled).

## Fingerprint and format recognition

* **Long pure-text lines (commentary, disclaimers) are included in the fingerprint**, so a provider whose statements contain changing prose may be re-learned every month.
* **A single renamed column barely changes the similarity score**, so the fingerprint cannot
detect it. Detection relies on the engine's missing-column check, which is why a renamed
column triggers a re-learn and not a DRIFT status.
* **Thresholds (0.85 match, 0.50 drift) are judgement, not tuned** on a real corpus.
* **Header cells containing digits are dropped** from the fingerprint (e.g. "Q1 Value"), and
short headings are joined with spaces, so the representation is a heuristic.
* **Currency words are stripped from labels**, so a currency change alone is not detected;
currency is read from the statement itself.
* **Two products of one provider with the same layout share one format**, and so would a
white-label template used by several providers.
* **A DRIFT layout that still parses is flagged but not registered**, so it is flagged again
every month until a human acts.

## Config language and engine

* **Header fields come from regexes over the whole document text, first match wins.** An earlier
occurrence of the same label elsewhere on the page would be captured instead.
* **No protection against slow regexes** (catastrophic backtracking) in an LLM-written config.
There is no timeout.
* **Summary values must be a line whose first cell is the label and whose last cell is the
value.** Values above labels, or two label/value pairs side by side, cannot be expressed.
* **Signs are recorded as printed.** Only the config's transform (`number_abs`, `number_drcr`)
decides the sign, so a wrong choice by the LLM flips an amount without any parse error.
* **One NAV per statement.** Several unit classes, several currencies, or per-tranche capital
are not supported. "Capital called to date" is printed by one sample and deliberately not stored.
* **Schema gaps:** realised vs unrealised gains, XIRR, sector, accrued interest and benchmark
returns are not captured.
* **Transaction types are matched by keyword.** An unrecognised label becomes `other`, which
validation reports as an error.
* **Day/month order is chosen by the config.** If the LLM picks the wrong date transform, only
the "transactions within the period" check can reveal it.

## Learning with the LLM

* **A learned config is proven on one document only.** It may overfit (e.g. a stop line that
works this month). Later statements are still validated numerically, so most breakage shows up
as `needs_review`, but a config that is wrong in a way that preserves the arithmetic would
not be detected.
* **Prompt injection is mitigated, not eliminated.** The LLM can only return data, the text is
delimited and marked as untrusted, and gates 3 and 4 reject configs that do not really parse.
A manipulated config that parses this document correctly but misreads others would pass.
* **Statement text is sent to a third party** (Gemini) the first time a layout is seen. It
contains the client ID, holdings and balances. The free tier may use prompts to improve
Google's products. Only synthetic data was used here; real use needs a data agreement and
redaction of identifiers before the call.
* **Prompts are capped at 400 lines or 40,000 characters.** A table past the cut cannot be learned.
* **One fictional example in the prompt.** Unusual layouts may fail all 3 attempts and end as
`learning_failed`.
* **A newly learned format is accepted automatically** (a warning only) unless `--review-new` is
used. A re-learned config for a changed layout is registered before a human confirms it, so a
wrong one would match future documents.
* **Availability:** during development the first model name was retired (404) and one call hit a
503 spike. Both are reported clearly; learning is paused, never skipped silently.

## Validation

* **Errors that cancel out are invisible** (two wrong holdings that offset each other).
* **A statement that prints little can pass trivially.** The report lists skipped checks (e.g.
Meridian has no reconciliation), but nothing fails because many were skipped.
* **Tolerance is 0.1% or 1 unit.** Reconciliation accepts two formulas (gain before or after fees),
which loosens it slightly.
* **Weights are compared against only two denominators** (closing value or holdings total).
* **Cost basis is never validated** (no independent figure to compare).
* **No continuity check across months** (opening value vs last month's closing).
* **The fee-total check is a warning, not an error.**

## Pipeline and storage

* **Deduplication is by file bytes.** The same statement re-issued as a different PDF is
processed again and can be stored twice.
* **Failed documents are not retried automatically.** After an email run, a `learning_failed` or
`password_required` statement needs the pipeline run over `data/attachments`.
* **Passwords come from a flat list.** An unlisted password leaves the statement
`password_required`, and a password containing a comma cannot be entered.
* **Statements are stored as JSON blobs**, so there is no cross-provider query and no
consolidated view for one client. Client identifiers are provider-specific and nothing links them.
* **SQLite, one process.** One lock around the connection; no migrations, workers or backups.
* **Unexpected exceptions become `failed**` with the exception text, so a bug in our code and a
bad document look the same on the review page.

## Email

* **Classification is keyword scoring.** A personal bank statement mentions "statement" and
passes; a real statement with no keyword in the subject, filename or body, from a sender not in
`STATEMENT_SENDERS`, is skipped. Skips are recorded and visible.
* **PDF attachments only.** Download links, password-in-body emails and other file types are ignored.
* **Only the first 2,000 characters of the body are read**, and HTML is stripped crudely.
* **IMAP with an app password** gives broad mailbox access. A production system would use OAuth
with a read-only scope. The system opens the mailbox read-only and never changes mail.
* **Metadata of every email seen is stored** (subject, sender), including unrelated ones.
* **Downloaded attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`.
* **Attachments over 25 MB are ignored**, and the search window is date-granular.

## Review interface

* **Access control is a single shared token** over plain HTTP, with no rate limiting. There are
no user accounts, so the review history records the decision and time but not *who*. Intended
for localhost only.
* **Reviewing confirms extracted data, not the learned config.** A re-learned config is
registered before a person confirms it; the page cannot approve, revert or edit a config.
* **Reviewers cannot edit data.** A wrong number can be rejected, not corrected.
* **Search is a substring match**; no pagination of emails or formats.
* **Updates are polled every 20 seconds.** An open detail panel is not refreshed.
* **The JavaScript has no automated tests** beyond two source checks (no HTML injection, no float
conversion). Layout was checked by hand.
* **The page can now run the pipeline.** Anyone with the access token can upload a PDF (25 MB
limit, must start with `%PDF-`) or fetch the mailbox, which can send that document's text to
the LLM provider. There are no per-user accounts, quotas or virus scanning.
* **Passwords typed into the page travel in an HTTP header over plain HTTP** (localhost only).
They are used for that one run, never stored or logged, and are not part of the URL.
* **Uploaded files and email attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`. Retry works only
for files saved there; a document processed from the command line must be uploaded again.
* **One job at a time.** A second request gets "another job is running". There is no progress
stream, so a slow LLM call shows only a spinner and the page must stay open.
* **Demo mode can wipe the database.** It only starts on a database whose file name contains
"demo", the reset needs a confirm dialog and the word RESET, and the demo files are generated
into `data/demo` (not into `samples/`).

## Testing

* **Every test uses five synthetic statements and a few variants I generated.** The configs, PDFs
and answer keys come from one author, so the suite shows the design is consistent, not that it
handles real-world statements.
